content.text:
We are running one discovery round to find stable, non-toxic solar absorbers (SLME ≥ 30%, ehull ≤ 0.05 eV/atom, no Pb/Cd/Hg/Tl/As) in the JARVIS-DFT dft_3d dataset (doi:10.1016/j.commatsci.2025.114063). Cheap descriptors: composition, OptB88vdW band gap, ehull, formation energy. Oracle: SLME (1 budget unit / material). Pool: 1,362 candidates; 129 hits; base rate 9.47%. Baseline (random): ~106 calcs to find 10 hits. Prior calculations available: 8,660.

Three agent-generated hypotheses to evaluate:

H1 — Cheap Pre-Filter (zero oracle cost, retrospective):
Apply: OptB88vdW gap ∈ [0.7, 1.2] eV AND direct-gap = True AND ns² cation ∈ {Bi, Sb, Sn, Ge, Cu}.
Claim: retains ≥75% of hits, eliminates ≥55% of non-hits → enriched hit-rate ≥15%, calcs-to-10-hits ≤50.

H2 — Heteroscedastic GP Surrogate:
Fit per-family noise (σ²_chalcogenide separate from σ²_halide, etc.) on 8,660 prior calcs.
Claim: Chalcogenide MAE falls from 5.37% to ≤3.8%; BO with this surrogate finds 10 hits in ≤55 calcs.

H3 — Two-Stage Pipeline (H1 → BO, the recommended test):
Chain H1 filter (→ enriched sub-pool ~50% of 1,362) with GP-BO on the enriched pool.
Claim: finds 10 hits in ≤30 calcs (≥3.5× vs. random); beats either stage alone by ≥1.3×.

Please design at least TWO candidate tests and pick ONE by expected learning, cost, and feasibility:
- For each candidate test, specify: exact steps, cheap descriptors used, oracle calls required (budget), expected outcome, and what it would teach the lab if it succeeds OR fails.
- Choose the one test with the highest expected information gain per oracle call.
- The runner will execute exactly the test you choose — be precise about the tool calls and parameters.

Note: The lab rule requires approval before spending >20 oracle calculations. Retrospective/simulation tests that spend zero oracle budget may run without approval. Please flag any test that would spend oracle budget.

Constraints: This is round 1; we want to establish a benchmark before spending real budget. Prefer zero-budget retrospective tests that validate the filter/model before any oracle spending.
